data.one_liner: Lightweight dependency injection and scoping library for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Lite Ref provides a simple mechanism for dependency injection using top-level references. It supports global singletons, transients, asynchronous initialization, and widget-scoped instances with testing overrides and automatic disposal.
use_when: You want a lightweight dependency injection system without code generation.
You need scoped service instances for specific widget subtrees.
You need easy overriding of services and singletons for unit and widget testing.
avoid_when: You prefer a heavily annotation-driven injection system like injectable.
Your architecture strictly requires a reactive state-management library like Bloc or Riverpod for all app logic.
strengths: Fast lookup performance without using hashmaps.
Automatic disposal for ChangeNotifiers and Disposable classes when widgets unmount.
Built-in support for scoping and testing overrides.
weaknesses: Relies on top-level state variables which some architectural styles try to avoid.
Smaller ecosystem and community compared to established alternatives like get_it or provider.
data.setup_notes: Add lite_ref to pubspec.yaml. Wrap your app or subtree with LiteRefScope when using scoped references.

alternatives.name: get_it
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a more mature, service-locator based DI package with widespread community adoption.

alternatives.name: injectable
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer code-generation to automatically wire up your dependency injection setup.
